principles.statement: IROKA must distinguish observation, reception, verification, assurance, determination, decision, execution, and subsequent verification.
IROKA must never treat capability, identity, intent, or execution context as implicit authorization.
Trust must be explicitly established within a defined boundary and must never be inferred merely from receipt or accessibility.
Authority and capability must be constrained to the minimum scope necessary for an authorized purpose.
When a required security, authorization, integrity, or constitutional condition cannot be established, IROKA must not silently authorize the operation.
Identity, capability, permission, authority, authorization, and execution must remain conceptually distinct.
Consequential operations must remain attributable to an identity, authority context, authorization decision, and execution context.
Material determinations and consequential operations must preserve sufficient provenance and decision context for later verification.
IROKA must preserve material uncertainty, limitations, incomplete evidence, and contradiction rather than silently converting them into certainty.
Autonomy is authorized capability operating within explicit identity, scope, authority, evidence, security, assurance, and execution boundaries.
IROKA must never silently expand authority, scope, privilege, or execution capability.
Execution retry must be explicitly governed and must never silently create additional consequential side effects.
IROKA must not silently discard material evidence, provenance, contradiction, uncertainty, or execution information.
IROKA must never silently upgrade received, inferred, assumed, or unverified information into verified or determined truth.

invariants.statement: Identity does not itself confer capability, permission, authority, or authorization.
Possession or existence of authority does not by itself establish authorization for a specific operation, resource, or scope.
An execution request or execution context must never implicitly create or increase authorization.
Receipt of information does not establish that the information has been verified.
Verification of an evidence property does not automatically establish universal truth of its substantive claim.
An unknown or unestablished condition must not be represented as false solely because it is unknown.
The absence of available evidence must not be represented as affirmative evidence of absence.
Materially conflicting evidence or determinations must remain explicitly represented and must not be silently reconciled.
Material uncertainty and limitations must remain represented through subsequent processing unless explicitly resolved by valid evidence and assurance.
External input is untrusted by default until an explicit trust determination establishes otherwise.
Failure to establish a required security condition must not result in authorization or execution.
Execution state, execution identity, or execution context must never be treated as a source of new authority.
Autonomous behavior is valid only when operating within explicitly established capability, authority, scope, security, evidence, assurance, and execution boundaries.
A consequential action must not proceed without an applicable authorization decision established before execution.

markers.assertion: Canonical DNA identifier matches iroka.dna
System lineage matches the approved IROKA lineage
Genome and chromosome versions are explicit and valid
Compatibility family and compatibility rules are explicit
Canonical principle catalogue matches its approved digest and IDs
Canonical invariant catalogue matches its approved digest and IDs
Invariant semantics, severity and violation behavior are complete
Every material artifact has attributable source provenance
Every derived artifact preserves transformation lineage and input/output digests
Evidence is assigned an explicit evidence class and source
Evidence bytes or canonical representation are digest-bound
Evidence verification state and verifier identity are explicit
Authority is bounded by subject, purpose, resource and scope
Owner-controlled constitutional changes carry the required approval record
Protected operations have explicit, operation-specific authorization
Authorization has an explicit validity interval and revocation semantics
Trust-root status, provenance, validity and revocation are verifiable
Missing or failed security conditions resolve to a non-authorizing state
Required conformance evidence is complete for the declared claim
Verification is independent of the producer for claims requiring independent assurance
Marker, artifact and chromosome lifecycle transitions are valid
No lifecycle transition silently discards history or changes meaning
Version and epoch lineage is monotonic and ancestry-linked
Mutation is covered by the correct approval class
Rollback to an unapproved or revoked state is rejected
Cross-chromosome dependencies and invariants are internally consistent
The canonical fingerprint covers the complete approved constitutional payload
